newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian MinFins firm further as Yeltsin feels good.
newsitem.headline: Russian MinFins firm further as Yeltsin feels good.

text.p: Prices of Russian MinFin bonds firmed further on Wednesday on President Boris Yeltsin's recovery from heart surgery and Russia's attempts to resolve the problem of frozen MinFins, dealers said.
Yeltsin resumed his presidential authority early on Wednesday.
And the government called on the judicial authorities to review recent freezes of MinFin bonds at a meeting on Tuesday.

A meeting chaired by First Deputy Prime Minister Vladimir Potanin also called for the legal authorities to draw up proposals within 10 days to remove discrepancies in Russia's criminal and civil codes affecting the bond freeze.
It also called on the Interior Ministry and Prosecutor-General's office to refrain from any actions which could damage bondholders' rights.
"Prices have been rising the whole day just because Yeltsin feels all right and is likely to return to work quite soon," one dealer said.
But dealers said the Russian government's attempt to resolve the problem of frozen MinFins was another optimistic sign for the market which has been overshadowed by the matter since last Monday.
"It is a very important and positive sign but it may be too early to speak about the reaction because of the holidays," a Moscow Narodny Bank dealer said.
"The question now is what the judicial authorities would come up with in 10 days," he added.
November 7 and 8 are holidays in Russia, marking the 1917 Bolshevik revolution, while Sunday will be a working day.
